sources.title: Resident Evil Requiem wins four Golden Joystick Awards, including Ultimate and Console GOTY
sources.text: Capcom receives seven awards, including Studio of the Year and recognition for Pragmata and Onimusha: Way of the Sword The 44th Golden Joystick Awards took place last night, with Resident Evil Requiem winning four awards including Ultimate Game of the Year and Console Game of the Year. The ninth instalment in the franchise also received Best Game Trailer, in addition to Angela Sant'Albano winning Best Lead Performer for her role as Grace Ashcroft. Capcom received seven awards, including Studio of the Year, Best Audio Design for Onimusha: Way of the Sword, and Best Supporting Performer for Grace Saif’s role as Diana in Pragmata. AdHoc's Dispatch earned Best Storytelling and Best Soundtrack. Meccha Chameleon was recognised as Best Indie Game (self-published), Best Multiplayer Game, Streamer’s Choice, and Developer’s Choice. Elsewhere, Remedy received Best Visual Design for Control Resonant, Unknown Worlds' Subnautica 2 won Best Early Access Game, Pearl Abyss's Crimson Desert was named PC Game of the Year, and House House's Big Walk received Critics' Choice. sources.name: PC Gamer
sources.title: Crimson Desert wins 'PC Game of the Year' at the 2026 Golden Joystick Awards
sources.text: Resident Evil Requiem and Meccha Chameleon were the night's other big winners. There was some fun conversation here at PC Gamer recently about the anachronistic name of The Golden Joystick Awards, which are put on by PC Gamer's publisher. Who even uses a joystick anymore? Flight sim diehards, fighting game enthusiasts, and not many others. So why is it called that? Joysticks , really? Simply put, the name reflects the age of the awards, which debuted in 1983, making it the longest-running publicly-voted videogame awards show of all time, according to Wikipedia. Back in those days, joysticks were it, and trust me, they weren't the sweet pieces of hardware we have access to now. But we loved 'em! And we used them to play games like the Golden Joysticks' first-ever game of the year, Jetpac. It was a banger! Here we are, 43 years later, and much has changed: From a tiny ceremony handing out five trophies, the Golden Joysticks have grown to become one of the biggest videogame awards events of the year, watched by millions of people around the world on just about every streaming platform you can name. Yet that name, the Golden Joystick Awards , remains. Frankly, I'm glad about that. A little bit of reliability in this world is good for everyone. Which leads me to the point: The 44 th annual Golden Joystick Awards has now concluded, and the top gong , as my UK compatriots like to say for some reason—the Ultimate Game of the Year award, for the rest of us—has gone to Resident Evil Requiem , Capcom's latest tale of zombie-fueled bad news. Can't really argue with that call: PC Gamer's Elie Gould gave Resident Evil Requiem a whopping 92% score in their review , saying it "feels like you're playing a highlight reel of the best moments in the series." Requiem claimed three other wins on the night: Console Game of the Year, Best Game Trailer, and Best Lead Performer for Angela Sant'Albano's turn as Grace Ashcroft. Crimson Desert won for PC Game of the Year, which surprises me a bit given that it's also on consoles and pretty much the same experience. We liked that one too: Not quite as enthusiastically, but it still earned an enviable 80% review score . "Vast and obtuse in a way that is going to frustrate some and exhilarate others," as reviewer Mollie Taylor put it: "A fascinating journey, even when the destination isn't all that." Multiplayer hide-and-seek game Meccha Chameleon was the night's other big winner, taking home four awards for Best Multiplayer Game, Best Indie Game (self-published), the Steamers' Choice Award, and Developer's Choice Award. Dispatch won twice, for Best Storytelling and Best Soundtrack, and The Witcher also sort of claimed two wins as well: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered took the trophy for Best Remake/Remaster, while The Witcher 4 won for Most Wanted Game. Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. So there you have it, 44 years down and hopefully many more to come—all of them bearing that glorious golden name. From there he graduated to the glory days of Sierra Online adventures and Microprose sims, ran a local BBS, learned how to build PCs, and developed a longstanding love of RPGs, immersive sims, and shooters. He began writing videogame news in 2007 for The Escapist and somehow managed to avoid getting fired until 2014, when he joined the storied ranks of PC Gamer. He covers all aspects of the industry, from new game announcements and patch notes to legal disputes, Twitch beefs, esports, and Henry Cavill. Lots of Henry Cavill. sources.title: Resident Evil Requiem actor after Golden Joystick Awards win: "Capcom, you cannot fail!"
sources.text: Resident Evil Requiem walked away with the biggest prize of the night at the Golden Joystick Awards yesterday, capping off a total of four wins with the prestigious title of Ultimate Game of the Year. But in an acceptance speech delivered on-stage by Leon Kennedy actor Nick Apostoledes, there was an allusion to an even bigger winner - Capcom itself. "What can I say?" Apostoledes began. "Resident Evil going 30 years strong this year - how fitting is it to win Ultimate Game of the Year for Requiem? We are just honored to be part of a project that is so beloved, a franchise that is so beloved. Thank you to the fans, thank you for keeping this alive. Capcom, you cannot fail." Apostoledes' remarks were followed up by pre-recorded comments from Requiem director Koshi Nakanishi, who said he was "thrilled" to accept the award, and spoke about how encouraging it was for a single-player game to win, especially in such a crowded field. While Resi itself will be making the big headlines, however, Apostoledes touched on an interesting point: the legendary run that Capcom itself is on. As well as claiming two GOTY titles for Requiem, that title also secured wins in the Best Game Trailer category, and a Best Lead Performer win for Grace Ashcroft actress Angela Sant'Albano. But two of Capcom's other titles - Pragmata and Onimusha: Way of the Sword - were also in contention for several categories, each one claiming its own win. Onimusha took the prize for Best Audio Design, while Diana actress Grace Saif took home Best Supporting Performer for her role in Pragmata. With three out of its four major releases this year claiming wins, perhaps it was of little surprise that Capcom would also take home the prize for Studio of the Year. 2026 has been a jewel in a crown that Capcom has been polishing for some time now. In the last four years, it's been on an excellent run. The last time a new release has slipped below a MetaCritic score of 80 was 2023's Exoprimal, and the closest thing it's had to a flop was Monster Hunter Wilds, which was plagued by performance issues. Elsewhere, it's been turning Resident Evil back into an essential release, breathing new life into classics, and successfully bringing life to new IP. It's been a relatively slow, quiet process, but Capcom has rarely put a foot wrong since 2020, and the community is starting to take note. 2027 looks like a quieter year for the studio, but with Resident Evil Veronica on the horizon, it looks like fans will still be eating pretty well. Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more I'm GamesRadar's Managing Editor for news, shaping the news strategy across the team. I started my journalistic career while getting my degree in English Literature at the University of Warwick, where I also worked as Games Editor on the student newspaper, The Boar. Since then, I've run the news sections at PCGamesN and Kotaku UK, and also regularly contributed to PC Gamer. As you might be able to tell, PC is my platform of choice, so you can regularly find me playing League of Legends or Steam's latest indie hit. sources.text: A Xbox Game Studios e a Playground Games divulgaram um novo vídeo de gameplay de Fable , reboot da tradicional franquia de RPG. A apresentação aconteceu nesta quinta-feira (12), durante as comemorações dos 25 anos do Xbox , e trouxe aproximadamente quatro minutos de uma missão inédita. O vídeo apresenta uma sequência de exploração na região de Deepwood, onde o protagonista investiga acontecimentos mágicos que estão afetando os moradores de Oakshire. O novo Fable tem lançamento previsto para 23 de fevereiro de 2027 , com versões para PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S e PC. A demonstração acompanha o Herói de Briar Hill, protagonista da aventura, ao lado de Arden, um herói local. Os dois entram nas profundezas de Deepwood para investigar fenômenos mágicos que vêm causando problemas aos habitantes de Oakshire. Durante a missão, os personagens encontram uma área onde a magia natural da floresta parece ter sido corrompida por uma força externa. A exploração também revela pistas sobre quem ou o que pode estar por trás dos acontecimentos, estabelecendo um dos mistérios que os jogadores deverão investigar. Segundo a descrição oficial da Xbox Game Studios, a sequência foi preparada especialmente para as comemorações de aniversário da marca. O material oferece uma nova amostra da ambientação de fantasia do RPG, que marca o retorno de uma das franquias mais conhecidas do Xbox. Desenvolvido pela Playground Games, estúdio responsável pela franquia Forza Horizon , o novo Fable representa um reinício da série de RPG criada originalmente pela Lionhead Studios. O jogo está previsto para chegar em 23 de fevereiro de 2027 , nas seguintes plataformas: A chegada ao PlayStation 5 também amplia a disponibilidade da franquia, historicamente associada aos consoles Xbox. Com a nova demonstração, a Microsoft continua apresentando detalhes do retorno de Fable , que terá uma nova interpretação do universo de fantasia de Albion. sources.name: Kotaku
sources.title: Take-Two CEO Says Discs Will Become Gaming’s Vinyl: ‘It’s Going To Be A Very Small Part Of The Business’
sources.text: Discs GTA 6 Physical Games PlayStation Rockstar Games Vinyl Grand Theft Auto 6 is the first major console game to release without a physical version. Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick doesn’t think it’ll be the last. Physical games will hang around, but not in any mass-market sort of way. He says they’ll become closer to the equivalent of vinyl records in music. âIt may not be the end, but listen, weâve been talking, you and I, for a long time,â he told The Game Business ‘ Christopher Dring in a new interview. âI predicted that digital distribution would be well over 90 percent of the business more than 10 years ago. I donât always get it right, but this one I got right. Will there always be some physical business? Yes, in the same way that thereâs still a vinyl business in recorded music. But itâs going to be a very small part of the business.â Physical music accounted for just over 10 percent of total music revenue in the first half of 2026, according to estimates by theÂ Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) . That comes out to $581 million, roughly 80 percent of which was earned through sales of vinyl. According to Circana , physical game sales in the U.S. last year hit a 30-year low of $1.5 billion. That was about 2.5 percent of the $60.7 billion consumers spent on âvideo game hardware, content, and accessoriesâ in 2025. Physical game sales are already a smaller chunk of overall game spending than vinyl is for music, and that’s before PlayStation game discs go away entirely in 2028. Game discs becoming vinyl would actually be a rosier outlook than where things currently seem to be trending. We still don’t know how Microsoft will approach physical media with the launch of its Project Helix family of next-gen consoles, and Nintendo has confirmed it has no plans to abandon physical games during the Switch 2 era, even if it’s already taken a half-step in that direction with game key cards. Will GTA 6 ever get a disc version? Vinyl has been a way for music lovers to immortalize their favorite albums. Surely the biggest game launch ever deserves something similar? Zelnick previously shot down rumors that GTA 6 wasn’t coming to disc. He’s now demurred on whether it could get a physical release in the future. That sort of âinformation always comes from our labels,” he told Variety this week, leaving the ball in Rockstar’s court to decide. GTA 6 is getting a vinyl release for its soundtrack , however. Seem a bit hypocritical? It’s probably less surprising when, as revealed in Take-Two’s latest financials, only 2 percent of its current revenue comes from game discs . sources.title: Take-Two boss isn't ruling out a GTA movie or TV show, but says they're "very, very selective" about who they work with
sources.text: A Grand Theft Auto movie could still happen one day With less than a week to go until the release of GTA 6 – aka the biggest entertainment release of all time – the boss of GTA publisher Take-Two isn't ruling out a GTA movie or TV show, but suggests one hasn't happened yet because they're "very, very selective" about who they work with. Speaking on The David Rubenstein Show , Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick was asked why, after 30 years and six mainline games, there still hasn't been a GTA adaptation, saying in response: "We're very careful about line extensions [adaptations in other mediums] because this is a creative company and our goal is to make the best entertainment on Earth. "We would make a movie or a television show based on our IP if our creative teams were passionate about it," Zelnick continued. "If they thought that would somehow engage and delight our consumers. It's a high bar to do that, and of course there's always the risk of failure. So we don't rule it out, but we're very, very selective." Video game adaptations are currently all the rage in Hollywood. 2026 alone saw the release of Resident Evil , Mortal Kombat 2, Street Fighter, Iron Lung, Exit 8, Return to Silent Hill, and the back half of Fallout season 2 , and 2027 looks to be even bigger for video games on screen with The Legend of Zelda movie , A Minecraft Movie 2 , Sonic 4 , and potentially a wave of TV shows set to release. GTA is a unique case, however, and given its scale, it's arguable that Rockstar and Take-Two would have more to lose than gain from a GTA movie or TV show if any adaptation can't live up to the medium-defining legacy of the games. That said, imagine a GTA movie directed by one of the crime movie greats – a Michael Mann or a Martin Scorsese. Could Rockstar resist if one of the legendary filmmakers who informed much of their work wanted to return the favor? For now, the closest we have to a GTA movie is the 2015 docudrama The Gamechangers, which stars Harry Potter's Daniel Radcliffe as then Rockstar Games President Sam Houser and depicts the legal battle with Florida attorney Jack Thompson over the supposed psychological effects of violent games. Rockstar, famously, weren't fans, tweeting : "Was Basil Brush busy? What exactly is this random, made-up bollocks?" As for GTA 6, the map for the long-awaited Vice City-set game just leaked , and it could be teasing a UFO Easter egg. For that and much more, head on over to our countdown to GTA 6 landing page. GTA 6 releases on November 19. For more, check out our list of the best video game movies , and our guide to all the upcoming video game movies and shows heading our way. sources.title: Doom studio id Software confirms it's working on a new game
sources.text: But, just as with the next Elder Scrolls game, "it'll be some time" before it's ready to share more. Doom developer id Software has confirmed that it's working on a new game, although in phrasing that might strike you as familiar, it'll be "some time" before it's ready to reveal anything. The new project at id was first announced by Xbox CEO Asha Sharma, who's been making a few posts on X today to mark the looming 25 th anniversary of the original Xbox console. "Few studios have shaped the first-person shooter genre as much as id Software," Sharma wrote. "Slaughter Mode comes to Doom: The Dark Ages - Revelations on Monday, and the team is already working on its next game." "Already" might be stretching it a bit: The studio's previous game, Doom: The Dark Ages , came out well over a year ago, although the Revelations expansion only dropped in July. Regardless, the studio replied to Sharma's post to confirm that yes, a new game is coming. "We're incredibly excited about our next project, a new game from our teams in Texas and Frankfurt, with game direction once again by Hugo Martin," the studio said. "It'll be some time before we're ready to share more but we can't wait for you to see what we're working on." If that rings a bell, you may be thinking of The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel, which was given an official subtitle earlier this month—eight years after it was first announced. Despite that passage of time, Bethesda warned that more waiting is in store , using exactly the same phrase as id: "It'll be some time before we're ready to share more." Of course id Software and Bethesda Softworks are both subsidiaries of ZeniMax Media, which is owned by Xbox, so maybe that shared turn of phrase isn't entirely surprising. It does feel a bit unfortunate, though. On the other hand, it's nice to have confirmation that id is in fact doing something new. The studio was hit hard by the Xbox layoffs in July, reportedly losing more than 130 employees , raising concerns about its ability to continue functioning as a standalone developer. Studio co-director Marty Stratton said in October that "there was a very deliberate effort [during the layoffs] to make sure that we were incredibly viable coming out of that across everything we do." Stratton also said id is now "working more closely with MachineGames than ever," leading to speculation that the two studios may be collaborating on Wolfenstein 3. sources.title: New Game from Doom studio and New Wolfenstein Announced
sources.text: Xbox has great news for Doom and Wolfenstein fans Xbox is celebrating its 25th anniversary this month, and it's been spoiling fans left and right. Xbox games like Minecraft , Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 , Gears E-Day , and more received celebratory freebies. Beyond the awesome free in-game items, players were lucky enough to get a few exciting announcements coming from Bethesda-owned studios, Id Software and MachineGames. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma took to X this Thursday to discuss improvements coming to Xbox, but that's not all. Sharma promoted the launch of Slaughter mode, an endless combat mode for Doom: The Dark Ages . In this mode, gamers will fight through increasingly stronger hordes of randomly selected demons to get a higher score and collect Skulls that can be exchanged for unique rewards. After each wave, they must decide whether to continue and risk all their progress or give up and try again later. The Slaughter Mode update for Doom: The Dark Ages is scheduled to be released on Monday, Nov. 16. It is free for players who own the Revelations DLC or those who got the premium edition or upgrade for Doom: The Dark Ages . Doom: The Dark Ages developer Id Software responded to Sharma's post about the update and announced that its teams in Texas and Frankfurt are working on a new game. It seems like the mystery game is still in the early stages of development, as Id Software was not able to share much, but it did confirm that it will be directed by Hugo Martin, who helmed The Dark Ages . That wasn't the only new game reveal that we got on Thursday. Sharma confirmed that Wolfenstein 3 is officially in production at MachineGames. This was expected, as last year, studio head Jerk Gustafsson confirmed that the Wolfenstein reboot was always envisioned as a trilogy . However, confirmation of development is still a huge leap from mere rumors and discussion. Both game announcements were short on details, so it's likely that they're still in the early stages of development. Nevertheless, it's great news for fans who were looking forward to more games from these studios. For now, we will have to wait to learn more, but thankfully, we have Doom: The Dark Ages ' new game mode to keep us busy.

sources.title: 21 original Xbox games are now on PC via backward compatibility
sources.text: There are now 25 classic Xbox games available on PC, and four have achievements Xbox has added 21 new original Xbox games to its backwards compatibility catalogue on PC. The Elder Scrolls 3: Morrowind, Star Wars Battlefront, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, TimeSplitters 2, and more have been added to the catalogue, bringing the roster up to 25 on PC . Four of the games available on the service will also have unlockable achievements. The following games will join the PC backward compatibility catalogue with achievements:Â Star Wars: KOTOR, Star Wars: KOTOR 2, Blinx: The Time Sweeper, and Conker: Live and Reloaded. You can unlock achievements for these games when playing on an Xbox console too. This announcement comes as part of Xbox’s ongoing FanFest. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma also used the event to reveal that id Software is working on its next game after Doom: The Dark Ages . Xbox will also be hoping that this earns it some goodwill in the gaming community, following a year full of layoffs . These layoffs are part of Xbox’s ongoing “reset”, which has seen multiple studios spun off, sold, or merged with others, such as Bethesda and Obsidian , who now work together. Others have seen a massively reduced headcount.

sources.title: QSSR arrives in Marvel’s Spider-Man 2, Control Resonant, The Finals, ARC Raiders, and Hell Let Loose: Vietnam
sources.text: Find out how developers including Insomniac Games and Remedy benefit from the upscaling tech. Six years after launch, PlayStation 5 is still getting better. Last month, we introduced Quick Spectral Super Resolution (QSSR), bringing AI-guided upscaling to the console you already own. Since then, there’s been a lot of interest from developers eager to try it out. We’re happy to announce that the next set of games is on the way, with updates rolling out over the coming weeks. Built on the same foundation as PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) on PS5 Pro, QSSR can deliver sharper details, cleaner edges, and more stable images than traditional upscalers. And because it shares its interface with PSSR, it’s a natural fit for games that already support PSSR. Here’s what the developers have to say about it. Marvel’s Spider-Man 2 featuring QSSR upscaling “Having seen great results integrating QSSR in Marvel’s Wolverine, our team decided to bring it to Marvel’s Spider-Man 2 as well, in an update that’s live now! We’re excited for players to swing back into our 2023 title and see QSSR’s exciting image stability and sharpness benefits in both Fidelity and Performance modes.” - Mike Fitzgerald, Head of Technology, Insomniac Games Control Resonant featuring QSSR upscaling Remedy Entertainment is bringing QSSR to Control Resonant on PS5, with noticeable improvements in image stability and fine detail. “It’s great to see PlayStation bringing the same kind of leap on the PS5 that PSSR brought to PS5 Pro. QSSR gives Control Resonant a much more stable and detailed image, and we’ve worked closely with Sony to have it ready in an update coming in December.” – Erik Jansson, Senior Graphics Programmer, Remedy Entertainment The Finals and Arc Raiders featuring QSSR upscaling “With the new QSSR coming soon to ARC Raiders and The Finals, we can deliver increased sharpness, better environmental clarity and overall visual improvements to even more PlayStation players. We are very happy to see Sony’s continued investment in PlayStation technology translate into meaningful improvements for all players, bringing more immersive experiences across the PlayStation ecosystem.” – Mikael Linderholm, Technical Art Director, Embark Studios “No Man’s Sky gives players an infinite procedural universe to explore. When every star in the night sky is a real solar system players can visit, we care a great deal about the quality of every pixel. The team has always been passionate about pushing the boundaries of technology on PlayStation. QSSR (Quick Spectral Super Resolution) allows us to render the universe in sharper, cleaner and more beautiful detail, while delivering the best possible framerate. Look for it in the next few weeks. It’s another step towards making the universe of No Man’s Sky even more immersive to explore.” Hell Let Loose: Vietnam featuring QSSR upscaling “We’re delighted to confirm that we are adding QSSR to Hell Let Loose: Vietnam on PlayStation 5 through an upcoming update. Console visuals are something our community has been passionate about, and QSSR will bring sharper, cleaner image quality to the battlefield, from dense jungle to the chaos of a full-scale firefight. We can’t wait for our PlayStation players to see the difference.” – Paul Rustchynsky, Game Director, Expression Games Like the upgraded PSSR on PS5 Pro, QSSR grew out of Project Amethyst, our ongoing collaboration with AMD. It’s another example of how that shared work continues to benefit players across platforms. Developers are just getting started, and we’re excited to keep working with them to bring QSSR to more games on PS5 in the coming months.
